rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE FIRE-FIGHTING CAPABILITIES OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS (LGUS) BY ALLOWING LGUS TO RETAIN HALF OR FIFTY PERCENT OF ALL TAXES, FEES AND FINES COLLECTED UNDER PRESIDENTIAL DECREES NO. ELEVEN EIGHTY-FIVE (PD 1185), OTHERWISE KNOWNAS THE FIRE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Local governments are aware and recognize that a number of functions under the Fire code are best left under a national authority since these functions are very specialized and would require economies of scale to be cost-effective and cost-efficient. These services and functions obviously require reosurces as well. However, this should never be at the expense of preparedness and responsiveness. We should never scrimp or penny-pinch when it comes to the lives of people and our constituents.

rows.author: A076
rows.title_full: AN ACT REDUCING THE EXCISE TAX ON CERTAIN PETROLEUM PRODUCTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 148 OF THE NATIONAL INTERNAL REVENUE CODE, AS AMENDED
rows.abstract: Rationale: The latest developments in the oil industry resulted to widespread clamor for immediate transport fare and wage increases, investigation to the tree big oil companies, and even a repeat of infustry regulation. Hence, to help reduce the impact od such fuel adjustments that can be aggravated by an impending increase in transport fare and wages, it is hereby proposed to reduce the specific taxes of regular gasoline, kerosene and diesel fuels so as to cushion off effects of further oil price adjustments in the world market.  This would be done temporarily in the interest of national economu and general welfare until such time that the oil prices in the international markket stabilize.
rows.status: Substituted by HB12592

rows.abstract: "Micro and Cottage Industries Development Act of 1999." Rationale: Recognizing that the envisioned alleviation of poverty and the problem of massive unemployment particularly in the countryside cannot be alleivated without strong economic activitiesat the grassroots level and that micro and cottage industries, being highly labor-intensive and a primary user of indigenous raw materials, have the highest potential for employment, self-employment and livelihood opportunities, it is hereby declared the policy of the State to give preferential attention to the promotion and development of micro and cottage industries, including livelihood and self-employed activities.

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE DEFINITION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7877, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE `ANTI-SEXUAL HARASSMENT LAW'
rows.abstract: This bill states that WHEN AN OFFER OF A SEXUAL FAVOR IS MADE BY A PERSON TO ANOTHER HAVING AUTHORITY, INFLUENCE OR MORAL ASCENDACY OVER THE OFFERER IN EXCHANGE FOR A FAVOR SOLICITED BY THE LATTER FROM THE FORMER, AND THE PERSON OFFERED OF SUCH SEXUAL FAVOR ACCEPTS THE SAME IN CONSIDERATION THEREOF, THE ACCEPTANCE OF THE FAVOR OFFERED SHALL CONSTITUTE SEXUAL HARASSMENT PUNISHABLE UNDER THIS ACT: PROVIDED FURTHER, THAT THE PERSON WHO MADE THE ACCEPTED OFFER SHALL BE DEEMED AN ACCOMPLISE TO THE CONSUMATION OF THE OFFENSE AND SHALL BE PUNISHED AS SUCH IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE PERTINENT PROVISIONS OF THE REVISED PENAL CODE AND SUBJECT TO THE DISCRETION OF THE COURT.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 1999-09-21

rows.abstract: Rationale: Today's P3,000.00 is good only for a month's fee for a not so decent room or a bachelor's pad. rows.title_full: THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENT ACT OF 1999
rows.abstract: "THE OMNIBUS INVESTMENTS ACT OF 1999". Rationale: This proposed legislation on the rationalization of investment incentives will pave the way for an incentive system that is consolidated and highly focused, cost-effective in promoting investments, time-bound and simple to administer. This rationalization is necessary in order to meet, among others, the following objectives: to address the intense competition for foreign direct investment in the Asian region; to bring the country's incentive schemes in line with those in the ASEAN; and to achieve harmony with the WTO agreements, particularly on subsidies and countervailing measures.
